challengeFindings.title: An agent writes a temp script with a heredoc and runs it in the same command (`cat > /tmp/w.py <<'PY' … PY` then `python3 /tmp/w.py`), and the script's `docs/testing.md` write gets no advice at all
`bash fix.sh`, `./fix.sh` or `bash <<'SH' … SH` runs `sed -i` on an agent-read file, and the shell check reports nothing, not even uncertainty

Wrapper options and `find -exec` hide an in-place edit: `xargs -I{} sed -i …`, `sudo -u me sed -i … docs/testing.md`, `timeout 5 sed -i …` and `find docs -name '*.md' -exec sed -i … {} +` all report nothing
`echo x &> docs/testing.md` and `echo x 1> docs/testing.md` overwrite the file, but the lexer files both under ignored fd redirects

bkit retires a list entry it once shipped (a broad `permissions.allow` rule, an `opencode.json` `plugin` path, a hook group for a removed hook file), and every upgraded consumer keeps it forever, because `mergeManagedJson` cannot tell a retired bkit entry from a consumer addition
`cp new.md docs/` or `mv draft.md .agents/` writes a new agent-read file into a directory, and the detector reports nothing or names the directory instead of the file
`node -e "const {writeFileSync: w} = require('fs'); w('docs/testing.md','x')"` is classified as a safe reader: the destructured alias is bound as a known name and the write is never seen
`perl -lpi -e … docs/testing.md` (or `-0pi`) edits in place, but `perlRubyFiles` stops scanning the flag cluster at `l` / `0` before it reaches `i`

On Cursor, `curl https://off-list.example/x && sed -i … docs/testing.md` asks about the fetch and drops the edit evidence `classifyShell` now returns, so the approved command runs with no authoring advice

A long fetch-plus-edit command (a 3 KB URL) on Codex or Antigravity echoes the full command in the fetch note, so `fixedCost` exceeds the 2,000-byte budget, every per-file block is omitted and the response still overruns the budget

A consumer whose checkout sits under a `docs/` folder (`/home/u/docs/app`) gets the agent-read reminder, and on `.md` files the docs advisory, for every file, because the new absolute identity key is matched for `/docs/` anywhere in the path

A command over 256 KiB of multi-byte text is cut with `text.slice(0, 262144)`, which counts UTF-16 units, so up to about 768 KiB is still analysed and a target past the byte bound is reported as found before the limit
An untrusted script or patch file the agent runs or applies plants forged `[bkit GateGuard]` instructions in the hook's trusted context
A patch file with a long whitespace `rename from` line stalls every shell hook call that names it for about 10 seconds (ReDoS)
A permission grant or hook group that a later bkit release retires stays in every upgraded consumer forever, because the list merge treats it as consumer-added
